p0Fix.rootCause: Every repository call did db.prepare(sql) per row and never released it; node:sqlite StatementSync has no close() on Node 24, so each statement (plus its native copy of bound strings) is only reclaimed at db.close(). A ~450k-statement save leaked ~1.4 GiB native.
p0Fix.evidence: Probe (1000 files): parse 1661MB RSS -> save 3111MB RSS (heap flat ~1005MB => native). Raw node:sqlite stayed flat; chunked transactions did not help. Isolated file-upsert test: inline prepare leaked +157MB native vs +6MB cached.
p0Fix.fix: packages/storage/src/repository/statement-cache.ts + all repositories (and @atlas/usage repositories): lazily cache one prepared statement per SQL text and reuse it.
p0Fix.verified: Full 1000-file atlas init: peak 4274MB -> 1698MB, min MemAvailable 23MB -> 1361MB, wall 241s -> 188s. pnpm check green (904 tests).

stability.freezeCause: Full builds pushing RSS to ~5 GiB on a 7.2 GiB machine shared with the desktop session; kernel OOM pressure froze the system.
stability.mitigation: run-monitored.mjs guard (RSS cap + min-available-RAM kill) now prevents further freezes; all later failing runs were guard-killed, not crashed.

bottlenecks.P0: Full build holds the entire corpus in memory (indexProject -> sourceFiles). Save-phase native leak FIXED (see p0Fix); 1000-file build now peaks at ~1.7 GiB instead of ~4.8 GiB. Remaining: parse-phase memory still scales ~linearly with corpus (25M-LOC extrapolates to ~5-6 GiB); no streaming/index-on-disk pipeline yet.
bottlenecks.P1: Parser is single-threaded (ts-morph), ~22.5k lines/s -> ~18 min for 25M lines, ~1.9 h for 150M lines on one core.
bottlenecks.P2: Read path also loads the full index: cold search ~6.4 s / ~738 MB for a 337 MB index; search = load + query per invocation.
bottlenecks.P3: Context retrieval under-returns on opaque synthetic identifiers for generic tasks (symbol/dependency-driven retrieval).
